- When sentiment is negative or near-zero in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to match true mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.7) over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate future prices; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–7 days ahead.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating 0.8 and -0.2); use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-cycle mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in final 5–7 days if sentiment remains positive or neutral.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model delays correction; force early downward adjustment (e.g., 1–2 days ahead) to match true price drop.
